findings.evidence: crates/oqueue-core/src/rate_governor.rs lines 42-44 ('Doc 04 §3 does not split GCS's ramp by read/write, so neither does this') and RateGovernor::new (seeds write_bucket and read_bucket from the same initial_per_sec for Ramping); docs/internal/product/backlog.md's M1.13 row repeats the same claim; compare docs/researches/04-object-storage-s3-gcs.md §3, 'GCS. Buckets start with roughly 1,000 object-write requests/s and 5,000 object-read requests/s of "free" IO capacity'. The three review rounds on this file (recorded in the M1.13 commit message) verified the token-bucket arithmetic exactly but never checked the Ramping policy's shape against the source it cites — a design-vs-research mismatch invisible to per-commit review of the arithmetic fix. Filed as M1.33.
findings.summary: RateLimitPolicy::Ramping uses one initial_per_sec for both op classes, on a doc-04 §3 citation the source contradicts: GCS's documented starting rates are 1,000 write/s vs 5,000 read/s, a 5x split.

findings.evidence: docs/internal/product/decisions/0010-object-store-ranged-get-delete-and-put-meta.md line 30 vs crates/oqueue-core/src/byte_range.rs's actual Bounded(Bounded) shape (fixed in commit 4f83f47, ADR left unedited); crates/oqueue-core/src/fault.rs line 15 ('[`crate::Error::Permanent`]') vs crates/oqueue-core/src/error.rs (no Permanent variant yet, correctly deferred to M1.15). Neither file was touched again in commits M1.9-M1.14. No gate runs cargo doc, so nothing catches the broken link. Low-severity documentation drift, left unresolved by design at each commit's own review; recorded here since a milestone checkpoint is the natural point to sweep 'defer until next touched' debt that never got touched.
findings.summary: Two review minors deferred 'until this file is next touched' (review.md rule 15) were never touched again within M1: ADR-0010 still documents the pre-fix ByteRange::Bounded{offset,length} bare struct-variant shape, and fault.rs's StormKind doc comment has a broken intra-doc link to crate::Error::Permanent (a variant that does not exist until M1.15).
